page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top with page number 471 at right. Chapter heading "CAP. IV." and an italic argument below it, then the body text. Signature "Gg 5" at the foot.

main_text.l: Solvuntur, quae Turrianus Gelasiane sententiae obji-
cit, & quibus probare nititur, Gelasium canones Apostolicos pro veris agnovisse.
Gelasium multa in suis epistolis, ac decretis ex
Apostolicorum canonum libro laudare, ac velut Ecclesiasticas
mo haec recitat {a}ex prima, mihi nona,
epistola {b}; De his autem, qui se ipsos abscindunt,

l.i: paterni canones evidenter sequenda posuerunt, quorum tenorem
sufficiat indidisse; Dicunt enim talia perpetrantes, mox ut
agniti fuerint, a munere clericali debere eos
secludi; quod modis omnibus custodire nos
convenit; quia fas esse nulli suppeditat, quicquam
constituerit sacram mercatos esse pretio dignitatem,
convictos oportet arceri, non sine periculo
tem damnatio Simonis, quam sacra lectio

main_text.l: testatur, involuit. Tertio & haec ex eodem

l.i: Ecclesiae nullis extantibus causis ad aliam pu-

marginalia.note: a Pro can. cap. 15. p.49. verf.

page.notes: Reference marks a, b, c, d are placed in the text as printed; the note texts are copied from the right margin. The drop-cap P is a woodcut initial. The text ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page with "fuerit," which continues onto the next page. Italic passages are marked in the text. Some italic words near the notes are read with doubt, notably "Pro" in note a and "Gel." in note b.
